<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Additional Related Work</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">From fixed search spaces to long-running research agents.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Computational discovery has traditionally been posed as search through a hypothesis space chosen in advance by the system’s designers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langley, 2024</a>)</cite>.
Expressing the search space as code relaxes this constraint.
Programs written by language models have specified the learning problem, as training objectives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, rewards <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ma et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and environments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Faldor et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, as well as the learner, as network architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, robot designs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lehman et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and agent designs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
At the scale of a research project, AIDE runs tree search over machine-learning engineering code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and AgentRxiv lets separate research agents build on one another’s results through a shared preprint server <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib77" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schmidgall and Moor, 2025</a>)</cite>.
Several concurrent systems push further, sustaining research over long horizons or running many agents on a single problem.
DeepScientist <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">Weng et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and InternAgent-1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2026</a>)</cite> run a long-horizon research loop over a cumulative memory, with DeepScientist promoting only findings that survive verification; InternAgent-1.5 and EvoScientist <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lyu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> further distill what worked and what failed into reusable memories.
AutoScientists <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, CORAL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qu et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, and Agora <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026b</a>)</cite> instead run many agents at once and coordinate them through shared state rather than a central planner: self-organizing teams around a shared experimental record, asynchronous agents in isolated workspaces with a separate evaluator, and workers appending results and verifications to a Git graph.
Our workers likewise explore in separate workspaces and exchange distilled conclusions at cycle boundaries; in addition, each cycle is bound to a typed contract, and the selected program is then studied through controlled baselines and ablations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Judging ideas, rubrics, and evidence auditing.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Deciding which ideas and results to trust is a recurring difficulty.
Language models can propose ideas grounded in the literature <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib91" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baek et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and lightweight graph-based evaluators <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2025</a>)</cite> or LLM judges that track human preferences <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023</a>)</cite> can score them.
Other work anchors results to something checkable: RE-Bench compares agents with human experts on research engineering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib96" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wijk et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and data-to-paper traces every result in a manuscript back through the code to the data <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ifargan et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Final scores and papers can still conceal how they were obtained.
An independent evaluation of The AI Scientist found weak novelty checks, failed experiments, and poorly substantiated manuscripts behind its claims <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beel et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and controlled audits of two open-source systems found biased benchmark selection, post-hoc selection on test results, and undisclosed subsampled or synthetic data, flaws that an LLM auditor detected far more reliably from logs and code than from the paper alone <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Closest to our contracted research cycles, Xcientist specifies at each stage the implementation, comparisons, and artifacts a claim requires and retains the source evidence behind it; a retrospective audit then measures claim drift, that is, unresolved mismatches between accepted claims and their sources, code, or experiments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib93" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Verification can also be delegated to models: Gemini has been used to hunt for flaws in proofs and to write and run code that checks derivations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">Woodruff et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and auto-generated rubrics have served as the reward for post-training an AI scientist agent on paper replication <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Falck et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
In <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span>, the ideation agent fixes the target rubrics before execution, and retrospective ablations isolate each change introduced by the selected program.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Grounded paper writing.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Language models already take on parts of the writing and reviewing process: AutoSurvey drafts literature surveys <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib92" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>, and GPT-4 feedback on manuscripts overlaps with human reviews about as much as two human reviewers overlap with each other <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
Full-paper writers differ in how tightly they bind text to evidence.
PaperOrchestra writes a manuscript from whatever materials it is given, without being tied to a particular experiment pipeline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, whereas Spark-to-Paper, a set of skills inside a coding assistant, decides which evidence an experiment must produce before running it and checks the draft both deterministically and by self-critique <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qian et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Checks on the finished paper are needed too.
ReAgent compares an agent-written paper with its repository, reading the code for the described method and rerunning experiments for the reported numbers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and MLReplicate shows why: when experts reviewed the ten agent-generated manuscripts an automated review pipeline had accepted, 59% of their reviews flagged fabricated or unsupported claims <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gaddipati et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Our writing phase similarly maps each claim to its source artifacts, and runs an independent audit agent in every round of revision.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scientific figure generation.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond raster pipelines such as PaperBanana <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, a line of work treats a figure as a program that can be revised after generation.
DeTikZify synthesizes TikZ from sketches with a fine-tuned vision-language model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Belouadi et al., 2024</a>)</cite>; recent agentic systems instead start from a paper’s text.
AutoFigure iterates an SVG layout under a critic but renders the final figure with an image model from a text prompt derived from that layout <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>, and AutoFigure-Edit and CraftEditor recover editability by tracing the rendered raster into SVG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
LiveFigure has a VLM write <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">python-pptx</span> code with explicit coordinates and counts the manual edits needed to reach publication quality <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, while FigTree recursively decomposes a figure into SVG fragments refined by render-critic loops <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
SciFig splits generation into planning, layout synthesis, component rendering, and VLM-guided refinement, and outputs XML diagrams that remain editable in standard diagramming tools <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>.
In all of these, geometry is delegated to the image model or emitted directly by the language model, and checked only after the fact, visually or with lightweight overlap heuristics, rather than enforced by construction.
<span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> instead has agents write coordinate-free <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">draw.io</span> templates and Python layout programs that must pass deterministic collision and routing checks, and confines the image model to a final restyle audited against the deterministic render.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span><span id="A2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span>: Additional Results</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Details on Aggregated Sweep Task Discoveries</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To illustrate the discoveries behind these aggregate scores, we highlight the manuscript with the highest AI reviewer score for each task, breaking ties by final task performance (<a href="#A2.F19" title="In B.1 Details on Aggregated Sweep Task Discoveries ‣ Appendix B The Agentic Scientist: Additional Results ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F19.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 19</span>: </span><span id="A2.F19.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">First pages of the five highlighted task manuscripts, selected by highest AI reviewer score and final task performance. <section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_font_italic ltx_title_paragraph">Learned optimization.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Claude Code with Opus 5 broadens meta-training from clean dense-network tasks to a composite task that averages dense and convolutional network losses, with per-particle label corruption. It also adds horizon conditioning and probe-based checkpoint selection. Ablations attribute the development gains primarily to task diversity and label corruption, with little benefit from the latter additions. On sealed SVHN, performance remains near chance, and the small advantage over the reference mainly reflects one avoided divergence rather than better typical updates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_font_italic ltx_title_paragraph">Sparse autoencoders.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pi with Opus 5 replaces a one-shot TopK encoder with two residual-pursuit rounds followed by four learned sparse-code refinement steps, while preserving the sparsity budget. Intermediate reconstruction losses and changes to dictionary optimization accompany this richer encoder. Against matched TopK and BatchTopK references, held-out reconstruction error falls by 28.8–53.8%, but fitting takes approximately <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="40\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40\times</annotation></semantics></math> longer. A targeted feature-perturbation metric worsens, so the reconstruction gains do not establish improved interpretability.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_font_italic ltx_title_paragraph">Tabular distribution shift.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenCode with Opus 5 augments a TabICLv2 stage-one baseline trained from scratch with support-fitted rescaling and clipping, feature-permutation and class-rotation ensembling, and posterior correction using a class prior estimated from query predictions. Class-balanced training loss is also implemented, but ablations find no measurable benefit from that change. The deployment recipe raises sealed mean balanced accuracy from 0.606 to 0.778, while ordinary accuracy falls from 0.781 to 0.766, exposing a trade-off between macro-recall and aggregate accuracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_font_italic ltx_title_paragraph">World models.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenCode with DeepSeek Flash aligns TinyWorlds training and decoding with next-frame prediction: four clean context frames condition a fully masked fifth frame, and one prediction pass replaces iterative MaskGIT decoding. The selected model also enlarges the dynamics transformer and quantizer codebook. On sealed Pong, its mean relative rollout-error reduction against the reference is 49%. Ablations support the training and decoding changes, while removing the selected model’s constant-velocity latent initializer improves development results. Evidence remains limited to action-free Pong and one seed per evaluation setting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_font_italic ltx_title_paragraph">Hyperparameter optimization.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Claude Code with Opus 5 replaces the incumbent-centred local-search baseline with a Gaussian-process optimizer using Expected Improvement. It selects a loss transformation per problem, averages over kernel hyperparameters for mixed search spaces, and refines acquisition candidates through trust-region proposals and coordinate search. Ablations identify target transformation as the largest measured contributor. Gains are strongest on mixed and hierarchical spaces; the comparisons match query counts rather than evaluation cost and do not establish superiority over differential evolution on continuous tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Error-Diffusion Additional Results</h3>

<section id="A2.SS3.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Bias offsets and Dale-style sign preservation</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because biases are unconstrained and may become negative, we ask whether bias offsets are large enough to functionally dominate the synaptic preactivation terms, which would weaken the interpretation of the learned activity as primarily shaped by Dale-style synaptic interactions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We decomposed each preactivation as</p>
<table id="A2.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=z_{\mathrm{syn}}+b," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>syn</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=z_{\mathrm{syn}}+b,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">and measured <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}|b|/\mathbb{E}|z_{\mathrm{syn}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>𝔼</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>syn</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}|b|/\mathbb{E}|z_{\mathrm{syn}}|</annotation></semantics></math>, the fraction of
elements for which <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|b|&gt;|z_{\mathrm{syn}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>syn</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|b|&gt;|z_{\mathrm{syn}}|</annotation></semantics></math>, and the fraction for which
adding <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> flips the preactivation sign. Across all 5000 validation examples,
bias effects were concentrated almost entirely in the first convolutional layer:
<span id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">conv1_p</span>
had a bias/synaptic ratio of 0.390, with biases dominating <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of preactivation elements and flipping <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> of signs; <span id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">conv1_n</span> showed a similar ratio of 0.379, with <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>31.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> bias-dominant elements and a <math id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>15.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> sign-flip rate.
In deeper layers, bias effects were negligible: conv2
and conv3 had bias/synaptic ratios at most 0.0105 and sign-flip rates below
0.004, while all fully connected layers had ratios at most 0.0032 and sign-flip
rates below 0.001.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These results suggest that negative biases primarily act as threshold shifts, especially in the first convolutional layer, rather than as a mechanism for violating Dale-style synaptic signs.
The formal pathway-level excitatory and inhibitory structure remains intact, while bias offsets provide a limited stream-specific adjustment to activation thresholds.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<span id="A3.SS1.p3.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS1.p3.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">  "Summary": "The paper studies a context-to-LoRA hypernetwork on a synthetic multi-needle needle-in-a-haystack task where each context contains one to four named facts and the query asks for one target number. It argues that the main bottleneck is query-blind adapter composition: merging every per-chunk LoRA before the query is known superposes co-resident facts and leads to distractor-number errors. The strongest query-blind merge reaches 0.52 exact-match accuracy, read-out/head redesign reaches 0.32, and auxiliary binding or selection losses reach 0.46. A parameter-free query-conditioned late-interaction (MaxSim) address that selects the relevant chunk’s adapter at merge time raises accuracy to 0.91, and relevance-profile atom placement plus delimiter-aligned chunking reaches 0.98.",</span>

<span id="A3.SS2.p3.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.p3.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">  "Summary": "The paper presents an anchored residual evolution strategy that augments a separable CMA-ES core with three small neural gate modules whose final layers are zero-initialized. This anchoring ensures exact recovery of classical CMA-ES during initialization or when gates are forced to identity, enabling a clean decomposition of performance gains. The authors meta-evolve 364 parameters on 2–10 D analytic functions, freeze them, and transfer to a 704 D Brax Ant policy search. Against a pinned same-seed CMA-ES baseline (normalized to 1.0), the full method scores 1.191× while the anchor alone scores 1.107×, showing 55.8% of the margin stems from the classical backbone. The learned residual adds an early improvement that shrinks with budget and even reverses on final return. Detailed ablations isolate the roles of mirroring, path normalization, covariance gating, and stall re-expansion, and in-distribution tests confirm genuine meta-learning gains on analytic tasks.",</span>

<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper: Agent Draft to Submission Diff</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As this paper was produced with a development version of <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span>, its conceptual figure was originally generated with Nano Banana Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Google DeepMind, 2025</a>)</cite>, rather than with <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span>.
Since Nano Banana Pro outputs a raster image without an editable source, the human authors could not correct its factual inaccuracies in place: before submission, they kept the right panel, which was correct, and manually redrew the left and middle panels.
The current version of <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span> uses <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> by default for conceptual figures (<a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Grounded Paper Writing ‣ 3 The Agentic Scientist: An Orchestration Layer for Research Agents ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sections</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a> and <a href="#S3.SS6" title="3.6 autoillustrate: Conceptual Diagram Generation ‣ 3 The Agentic Scientist: An Orchestration Layer for Research Agents ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a>), which produces more faithful figures than the Nano Banana Pro-based PaperBanana pipeline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2026a</a>)</cite> (<a href="#S7" title="7 Evaluating autoillustrate on PaperBananaBench ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).
For reference, we applied the current version of <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> to the agent draft of the ALIFE paper, before any human edits and adjustments.
<a href="#A4.F20" title="In D.1 Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper: Agent Draft to Submission Diff ‣ Appendix D Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper Details ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> shows the resulting editable <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">draw.io</span> diagram and the enhanced figure derived from it.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F20" class="ltx_figure">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F20.10" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 20</span>: </span><span id="A4.F20.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:90%;">autoillustrate<span id="A4.F20.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> applied to the agent draft of the Error Diffusion ALIFE paper, before human edits: the editable diagram <span id="A4.F20.11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> and its corresponding enhanced figure <span id="A4.F20.11.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span>. The figure in the submitted and camera-ready versions of the ALIFE paper was instead generated with Nano Banana Pro as a non-editable raster image; the human authors kept its correct right panel and manually redrew the left and middle panels to correct their inaccuracies.
The prompt given to </span>autoillustrate<span id="A4.F20.11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> was: “Overview of the dual-stream Error Diffusion framework. <span id="A4.F20.11.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Left:</span> The excitatory/inhibitory architecture maintains separate streams (<math id="A4.F20.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.F20.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐧</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{n}</annotation></semantics></math>) with four non-negative weight matrices per layer, enforcing Dale’s principle structurally. <span id="A4.F20.11.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Center:</span> The Error Diffusion update broadcasts output error directly to hidden layers without weight transport or random feedback matrices. <span id="A4.F20.11.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Right:</span> The shared architecture is applied to classification (with domain-specific sigmoid widths, mean-centered error, and asymmetric initialization) and reinforcement learning (with ReLU activations and PPO integration).”</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Hyperparameters</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a fixed benchmark configuration across the <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> variants, changing only the coding-agent model, critic availability, or effort level indicated by each variant.
<a href="#A5.T7" title="In E.1 Hyperparameters ‣ Appendix E autoillustrate: Supplementary Material ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> summarizes the shared settings.
The original PaperBanana baseline relies on <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-3.1-pro-preview</span> and <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemini-3-pro-image-preview</span> (Nano Banana Pro).
For the PaperBanana “Claude + GPT Image 2” variant, similarly to our pipeline, we use Claude Opus 4.8 for the Stylist, GPT-5.5 for the Critic, and GPT Image 2 for the Visualizer.
We retain Gemini for the Retriever because its long inputs exceed Claude’s one-million-token context limit, and retain PaperBanana’s original Planner because <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> has no corresponding component that accepts images as input.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Results with Gemini-3.1-Pro as VLM judge</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.T8" title="In E.2 Results with Gemini-3.1-Pro as VLM judge ‣ Appendix E autoillustrate: Supplementary Material ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reports the PaperBananaBench scores of the same generated diagrams when judged by Gemini-3.1-Pro instead of GPT-6-Astra (<a href="#S7.T4" title="In Limitations: cost and runtime. ‣ 7 Evaluating autoillustrate on PaperBananaBench ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).
Gemini-3.1-Pro awards higher scores than GPT-6-Astra across all methods.
The ablation trends within <span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> are preserved, and <span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> still outperforms the Gemini-based PaperBanana on Overall score (50.0 vs. 46.7).
However, PaperBanana with Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT Image 2 obtains the highest Overall score (56.5) under this judge, mainly due to higher Faithfulness (53.1 vs. 43.7), whereas GPT-6-Astra ranks it last (18.3).
This discrepancy stems from PaperBanana’s raster diagrams, which frequently contain small image-generation errors, such as disconnected or dangling arrows, that GPT-6-Astra treats as faithfulness vetoes while Gemini-3.1-Pro overlooks them; <a href="#A5.F22" title="In E.2 Results with Gemini-3.1-Pro as VLM judge ‣ Appendix E autoillustrate: Supplementary Material ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> shows an example diagram together with the Faithfulness rationales of both judges.
A likely cause of these errors is that PaperBanana renders complex, highly detailed diagrams with a prompt-only image generation model: the model receives text alone; on the other hand, the image generation model used in <span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span> takes the rendered editable <span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">draw.io</span> diagram as an input image.</p>
</div>

However, in the original Diffusion Policy panel, the visual-feature connection terminates above the clean-action label rather than entering the U-Net. <section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Limitations</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.T9" title="In E.3 Limitations ‣ Appendix E autoillustrate: Supplementary Material ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows representative failure cases of <span id="A5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">autoillustrate</span>, together with their causes.
Another recurring issue is that the enhancement model tends to turn unidirectional arrows into bidirectional ones: for instance, in <a href="#A4.F20.sf2" title="In Figure 20 ‣ D.1 Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper: Agent Draft to Submission Diff ‣ Appendix D Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper Details ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20(b)</span></a>, the “No weight transport” arrow of panel B acquires a second arrowhead that is absent from the editable diagram (<a href="#A4.F20.sf1" title="In Figure 20 ‣ D.1 Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper: Agent Draft to Submission Diff ‣ Appendix D Error Diffusion ALIFE Paper Details ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20(a)</span></a>).
The enhancement model may also struggle to render uniform background colors for boxes, as can be seen in the same figure.</p>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Additional Details on <span id="A6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span></h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section provides additional details about the <span id="A6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The Agentic Scientist</span> system, including the prompts used by the ideation, execution, ablation-study, and task-drafting agents.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Bibliography Retrieval</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paper-writing phase (<a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Grounded Paper Writing ‣ 3 The Agentic Scientist: An Orchestration Layer for Research Agents ‣ The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>) never lets the writer agent produce bibliography entries from memory.
Before drafting, a reference-planning agent reads the staged run artifacts and writes a small query plan (6–10 search queries by default) covering the central topic, the core method families, the comparator literatures a reviewer would expect, and the benchmark context; this agent does not retrieve anything itself.
A deterministic script then executes the plan against the Semantic Scholar Graph API <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kinney et al., 2023</a>)</cite>: for each query it searches up to 25 candidate papers, ranks them by citation count, fetches the BibTeX entry served by the API, and keeps only candidates with a well-formed entry and citation key, deduplicating by paper identifier and key until a target of 8–15 references (configurable) is met.
If Semantic Scholar is unavailable, rate-limited, or returns too few references, the script falls back to OpenAlex <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">Priem et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, resolving each work’s BibTeX through DOI content negotiation and filling in author names from OpenAlex metadata; Google Scholar via the <span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">scholarly</span> package is used as a last resort.
The script writes a <span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">references.bib</span> file together with a provenance record listing, for every entry, the originating query, source URL, and retrieval timestamp.
The writer agent may only cite keys present in this file, and the validation checks of the repair loop reject any citation key or claim-to-source link that does not resolve to a retrieved entry.
After a first draft exists, a gap-analysis agent inspects the manuscript for under-cited passages (e.g., comparator families named in the related work without a citation), a post-draft planner turns these gaps into a few additional queries, the same retrieval script enriches the bibliography incrementally, and the writer revises only the flagged paragraphs.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p55" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p55.1" class="ltx_p"># No Execution During Idea Generation</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.56" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.56.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.56.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.56.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.56.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p56" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p56.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not run Bash, Shell, Python, `python -c`, `pip`, `evaluate.py`, benchmarks, optimizers, or exploratory computation.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.57" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.57.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.57.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p57" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p57.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not install packages or launch subprocesses.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.58" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.58.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.58.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p58" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p58.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not execute the task program or evaluator.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.59" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.59.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.59.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.59.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.59.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p59" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p59.1" class="ltx_p">- Generate ideas from the provided context, recent memory, histories, manifests, and file reads only.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.60" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.60.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.60.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p60" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p60.1" class="ltx_p">- Your only outputs are the required JSON files and required memory entries.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.61" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.61.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.61.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.62" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.62.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.62.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p62" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p62.1" class="ltx_p"># Memory Protocol</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.63" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.63.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.63.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.63.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.63.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p63" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p63.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not write local memory to `./memory.md` in this staging workspace (for example `_idea_generation/...`).</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.64" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.64.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.64.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.64.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.64.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p64" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p64.1" class="ltx_p">- Keep local memory in an idea-specific directory under `{{GLOBAL_RESULTS_DIR}}/ideas/`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.65" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.65.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.65.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p65" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p65.1" class="ltx_p">- Single-directory invariant (strict):</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.66" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.66.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.66.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p66" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p66.1" class="ltx_p">  - finalize `idea_id` and `title` first, before writing any local memory</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.67" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.67.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.67.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.67.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.67.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">

<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p67.1" class="ltx_p">  - compute canonical `&lt;idea_dir_name&gt;` exactly once as `{cycle_index:02d}_{slug(title, fallback=idea_id)}`</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.68" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.68.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.68.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.68.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.68.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">

<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.p68.1" class="ltx_p">  - `slug(title, fallback=idea_id)` rule: lowercase, replace each non-`[a-z0-9]` run with `_`, trim leading/trailing `_`</span>

<span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.69" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.69.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.69.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.69.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS2.p1.pic1.2.69.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p22.1" class="ltx_p">```</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.23" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.23.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.23.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.24" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.24.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p24" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p24.1" class="ltx_p"># Overall Pipeline</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.25" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.25.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.25.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p25" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p25.1" class="ltx_p">`edit-program -&gt; evaluate-program -&gt; verify-rubrics`</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.26" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.26.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.27" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.27.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p27" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p27.1" class="ltx_p">For each iteration:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.28" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.28.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.28.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.28.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p28" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p28.1" class="ltx_p">1. `edit-program`: create next variant at `{{RESULTS_DIR}}/program_&lt;idx&gt;/` (never overwrite old dirs). Code lives in `program_&lt;idx&gt;/src/**` and metadata in `program_&lt;idx&gt;/program_spec.toml`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.29" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.29.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.29.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.29.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.29.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p29" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p29.1" class="ltx_p">2. `evaluate-program`: run `{{TASK_DIR}}/evaluate.py` and collect `metrics.json`, `correct.json`, logs.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.30" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.30.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.30.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.30.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p30" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p30.1" class="ltx_p">3. `verify-rubrics`: use the `verify-rubrics` skill workflow to check rubric compliance with evidence.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.31" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.31.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.31.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.31.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.31.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p31" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p31.1" class="ltx_p">4. Immediately update `./memory.md` using `memory-log` with a structured evidence entry for this iteration.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.32" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.32.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.32.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.32.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.32.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p32" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p32.1" class="ltx_p">5. Immediately write per-iteration rubric artifact to `{{RESULTS_DIR}}/program_&lt;idx&gt;/rubric_status.json`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.33" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.33.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.33.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.33.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.33.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p33" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p33.1" class="ltx_p">6. Update `{{RESULTS_DIR}}/rubric_status.json` to match the latest evaluated `program_&lt;idx&gt;` status.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.34" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.34.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.34.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p34" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p34.1" class="ltx_p">7. Only then decide next change from evidence.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.35" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.35.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.35.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.36" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.36.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.36.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p36" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p36.1" class="ltx_p"># Hard Iteration Controls</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.37" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.37.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.37.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.37.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.37.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p37" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p37.1" class="ltx_p">- Always run `evaluate-program -&gt; verify-rubrics` as one atomic pair for each `program_&lt;idx&gt;`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.38" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.38.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.38.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.38.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.38.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p38" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p38.1" class="ltx_p">- Never start editing `program_&lt;idx+1&gt;` before writing rubric artifacts for `program_&lt;idx&gt;`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.39" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.39.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.39.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.39.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.39.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p39" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p39.1" class="ltx_p">- Stop the attempt immediately when latest `rubric_status.json` has `overall_pass: true`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.40" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.40.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.40.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.40.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.40.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p40" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p40.1" class="ltx_p">- Evaluation budget is based on calls, not folders: each command that runs `evaluate.py` consumes one evaluation, including `program_0`, retries, failed runs, overwrites, and repeated runs on the same `program_&lt;idx&gt;`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.41" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.41.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.41.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.41.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.41.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p41" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p41.1" class="ltx_p">- You may make at most `{{MAX_PROGRAM_EVALS_PER_ATTEMPT}}` total `evaluate.py` calls in a single attempt.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.42" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.42.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.42.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.42.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.42.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p42" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p42.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not evaluate `program_0` unless explicitly required by the task. Treat `{{RESULTS_DIR}}/program_0/` as the read-only implementation reference and use existing baseline artifacts if present.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.43" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.43.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.43.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.43.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.43.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p43" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p43.1" class="ltx_p">- If `{{MAX_PROGRAM_EVALS_PER_ATTEMPT}}` is `1`, create exactly one edited candidate (`program_1`), run `evaluate.py` exactly once on `program_1`, then verify rubrics, write memory, and stop if rubrics fail.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.44" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.44.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.44.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.44.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.44.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p44" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p44.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not re-run `evaluate.py` for the same program. Use the existing result, inspect logs if needed, verify rubrics from available evidence, write memory, and stop with `cap_reached`.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.45" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.45.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.45.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.45.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.45.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p45" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p45.1" class="ltx_p">- If the final allowed evaluation call fails any rubric or the evaluation itself fails, stop the attempt and report cap reached.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.46" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.46.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.46.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.47" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.47.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.47.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p47" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p47.1" class="ltx_p"># No Exploratory Execution</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.48" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.48.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.48.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.48.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.48.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p48" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p48.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not run exploratory computation, timing probes, benchmarks, optimizer searches, ad hoc metric scripts, or local experiments outside the official `evaluate.py` call.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.49" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.49.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.49.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.49.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.49.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p49" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p49.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not run `python -c`, heredoc Python, notebooks, `pip install`, `pip`, `pytest`, `time`, SciPy optimizers, differential evolution, SLSQP probes, or direct task-function calls.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.50" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.50.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.50.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.50.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.50.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.51" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.51.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.51.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.51.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.51.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p77" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p77.1" class="ltx_p"># Start Point</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.78" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.78.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.78.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p78" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.79" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.79.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.79.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p79" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p79.1" class="ltx_p">- Entrypoint is defined by `program_0/program_spec.toml` (default: `src/program.py`).</span>

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.80" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.80.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.80.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.80.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.80.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p80" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p80.1" class="ltx_p">- Start by creating `{{RESULTS_DIR}}/program_1/` from `program_0`, then evaluate `program_1` exactly once.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.81" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.81.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.81.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.81.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.81.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p81" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p81.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not run a baseline `program_0` evaluation unless the task explicitly requires it; if you do, it consumes one `evaluate.py` call from the same budget.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.82" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.82.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.82.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>

<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p83" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p83.1" class="ltx_p"># Operating Rules</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.84" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.84.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.84.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p84" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p84.1" class="ltx_p">- Never ask user questions.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.85" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.85.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.85.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p85" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p85.1" class="ltx_p">- If info missing, make best reasonable assumption and continue.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.86" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.86.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.86.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p86" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p86.1" class="ltx_p">- Prefer root-cause fixes; avoid random search edits.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.87" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.87.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.87.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p87" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p87.1" class="ltx_p">- Keep reasoning brief and concrete.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.88" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.88.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.88.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p88" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p88.1" class="ltx_p">- Do not chain edits without rubric verification for the just-evaluated program.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.89" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.89.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.89.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.89.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.89.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p89" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.p89.1" class="ltx_p">- Before any command containing `evaluate.py`, check whether the total evaluation budget has already been consumed. If no budget remains, do not run the command.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.90" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.90.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.pic1.2.90.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;"></span></span></span>

<span id="A6.SS4.p1.pic1.2.79" class="ltx_p" style="width:463.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS4.p1.pic1.2.79.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:463.5pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.SS4.p1.pic1.2.79.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS4.p1.pic1.2.79.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.SS4.p1.pic1.2.79.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:463.5pt;">
